newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel urges liberalising oil product exports.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel urges liberalising oil product exports.

text.p: A Japanese energy panel suggested on Monday that restrictions on oil product exports be removed and that a number of other measures be taken to improve efficiency in the oil industry.
The panel, an advisory body to the trade minister, suggested in a report that oil product exports be liberalised by September.
Japanese companies can currently export oil products only if they receive prior permission from the Trade Ministry.
In the report, the panel also urged that procedures to register new petrol stations be simplified.
The panel also called for a study on the possibility of launching a futures market in Japan in either crude oil or oil products, in order to increase the transparency of the market.
Japan implemented a deregulation scheme on April 1, 1996 that allows companies other than oil firms to import oil products.
The move has exposed the domestic industry to stiffer competition and has led to razor-thin margins for oil companies.
